title: How do you balance progression when AI writes most of your code? I ended up letting a bot play my game
author: Noah__1302
selftext:
I’ve been building a small incremental game with Claude doing most of the coding, and balancing turned out to be the hardest part. Tweaking numbers and playing for 20 minutes to see if it feels right just doesn’t scale when the AI can change ten values in a minute.

What I ended up doing: the game logic is completely separated from rendering, so a bot can play the whole progression headless in a few minutes. Every stage has a target time, and the bot should hit about 80% of it, since humans are slower. It also logs “dry streaks”, runs in a row where nothing was affordable, because more than two in a row feels like grind.

It works surprisingly well for pacing, but it obviously can’t tell me if something is fun. So I’m curious how others handle this. Do you playtest everything by hand? Simulate? Let the AI reason about the numbers directly? And has anyone found a good way to catch “technically balanced but boring”?
